notes.title: 30% off Brokk ship components
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/6c64aa6d03c7b8c03503cea1b6b4aa6f569516c8.png"][/img][/p][p]Pilots! It's time to improve your fleet strength! The Empire liaison at UMC reports that a new transport convoy has arrived in fringe sectors from inner worlds. It seems that the blockade has been broken. We are expecting even more trade caravans in the fringe sectors soon![/p][p][/p][p]Only today, September 24, we offer a 30% discount on Brokk components! They can be purchased directly from the ship tree.[/p][p][/p][quote][p]Externally Brokk is very similar to an imperial support cruiser, so the frigate has a very serious, aggressive and brutal look. This made it a full-fledged "imperial" dream for most pilots. It can rightly be called the most versatile engineering frigate and win in every possible category. There are going to be no obstacles for you — the special module will destroy all enemy ships in your way.[/p][/quote][p][/p][p][b]The special offer is valid for a limited time and will end on September 25![/b][/p][p][/p][p]Sincerely,
Star Conflict Team[/p]

notes.title: Star Conflict 1.13.10 Hotfix
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/b6e3774ecd51f8e0b082702636c6acf69145ac57.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Pilots! We have released a small update for the game with the following fixes:[/p][list][*][p]Active module “Suppressing sphere” no longer crashes ships under its effects.[/p][/*][*][p]Asteroids now drop the correct number of containers for players who have the “Asteroid conqueror” special license.[/p][/*][*][p]The conditions of some assignments of the “Way of kindness” marathon have been changed:[/p][list][*][p]“Kind killer” — the number of allies that you have to protect is now 35 instead of 75;[/p][/*][*][p]“Bomb carrier caretaker” — the number of enemies you have to destroy is now 15 instead of 25;[/p][/*][*][p]“Not today, I say” — The number of “NOT TODAY!” medals that you have to earn is now 2 instead of 5.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug that prevented the “Destroyed station” sector from being captured in the “Sector conquest” game mode.[/p][/*][/list]

Credits + 50%.[/p][list][*][p]Contains a 50% credit bonus for 24 hours.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][p][/p][hr][/hr][h1]Jericho rank 17 long-range frigate Carolingian[/h1][previewyoutube="8YoDlYdbQnM;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Carolingian-like ships were first spotted in 4624, when drone fleets attacked UMC convoys. In addition to standard interceptors and fighters, the insane artificial intelligence also used frigates of unknown design. It was these ships that caused significant damage, destroying transport escorts. Further inquiries to Jericho yielded no information, and the UMC command decided to study the new ships. During subsequent battles, enough samples were captured for the UMC engineers to recreate the long-range frigate, which they named Carolingian. Although it is only a copy, tests have shown significant similarities in combat parameters. The main difference is the increase in size due to the need to accommodate the larger onboard equipment.[/p][p]With truly powerful weapons, the Carolingian also has features akin to suppression destroyers, making the frigate particularly dangerous in combat. Currently, all UMC mercenaries can apply to receive the new ship.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h1]New modules by the “Atlas” Weapon Factories[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/7cd7f202ed3624f686fb7b1c769853c56f42f55c.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="justify"]“Atlas” is a new corporation that recently entered the weapons market. The line of exclusive arms it presented has shown itself perfectly in battle, having different capabilities from the standard weapon modifications. There is some reason to believe that the corporation uses mostly basic civilian components to assemble the weapons, achieving high performance with a few high-tech parts. Some speculate about the corporation’s connection to a civilian company that existed on Earth at the time of the Invasion. Since the fate of Earth is not fully known at this point, there can be no evidence of such a connection.[/p][p][/p][p]The new battle pass “Desolate worlds” has three brand-new modules for you:[/p][list][*][p][b]“Electromagnetic destabilizer” CPU modifier[/b] increases critical chance and upon activation lowers the hull resistance to electromagnetic damage for the selected enemy ship.[/p][/*][*][p][b]“Thermal destabilizer” CPU modifier[/b] increases critical chance and upon activation lowers the hull resistance to thermal damage for the selected enemy ship.[/p][/*][*][p][b]“Kinetic destabilizer” CPU modifier[/b] increases critical chance and upon activation lowers the hull resistance to kinetic damage for the selected enemy ship.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][hr][/hr][h1]“Way of Kindness” marathon[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/14c6fcbcf1ccf3923714d818bb418bc843fd7f8c.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Pilots! notes.title: Interview with a designer of the “Return of the Precursors” adventure
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/c1713cbde6387ebefcf097eb27b51007d119a489.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Pilots! The “Return of the Precursors” adventure has concluded, and we hope that it managed to please you in one way or another, whether with its challenging assignments, new activities in the open world, or plot development. As promised earlier, we invite you to read a unique retrospective: an interview with one of the designers of the adventure! We hope that many of the decisions made in the course of creating this event will become clearer to you, and you will be able to look at your personal experience of completing the adventure from a different perspective.[/p][p][/p][h2]Why did the adventure end, and why did it end so suddenly?[/h2][p]One of the volleys of the dreadnought “Defiant” (after the “Conquistador” had been weakened by a barrage of dissonant missiles) managed to pierce the hull of the Precursors’ flagship, causing a short circuit (one of the main power lines ran through the walls of the main deck) — this is the official version of events based on a lengthy analysis of the ship’s structure. One can only guess how many valuable items might have been among the wreckage of the destroyed ship! This can only be estimated by looking at the findings in the wreckages of turrets, destroyed after the “Defiant’s” volley! But it is now almost impossible to reach these treasures: everything has been swallowed up by the supermassive black hole of the Anomaly that remains in the place of the “Conquistador”... According to UMC reports, some mercenaries have already gone missing in attempts to reach the wreckage.[/p][p]Although the end of the adventure may seem sudden, there were enough signs of its imminent conclusion during the battle with the Precursors. First, there were significantly fewer Guardians, then the “Defiant’s” main weapon was activated and began to fire devastating shots. Dissonant ammunitions were developed and began to be used (with varying degrees of success)... We hope that many pilots quickly figured out which way events were actually going.[/p][p][/p][h2]Were the goals of the adventure achieved, and what did you want to accomplish?[/h2][p]We believe that the goals have been achieved. Of course, there were some deviations from expectations in a number of areas, but that’s normal; after all, we are dealing with a living community of sometimes completely different people.[/p][p]This adventure was designed to give players something new, to introduce a certain “challenge,” to force them to mobilize their reserves of knowledge and skills, to introduce some cool (or at least “unfamiliar”) mechanics into the game, to incentivize communication by trying to unite and encourage pilots to share information and interact, while not directly forcing them into teams. We understand that many play “solo”, and those who want more communication have long since taken their place in corporations. However, let’s take it one step at a time.[/p][p]The first thing to be said is that the “raid” format itself is unconventional. There is no “straightforward race” with a prize at the finish line. Practically the entire prize fund was not concentrated in one reward for the final task (“fly through the stages and get your handful of crystals and a box of currency”), but was distributed over the open world and was available to receive depending on player activity.[/p][p]A fairly simple cycle was created:[/p][olist][*][p]complete assignments;[/p][/*][*][p]receive resources (dissonant ammunition);[/p][/*][*][p]use the resources to obtain valuables in the Inverter by fighting the Precursors.[/p][/*][/olist][p]There were two ways to obtain resources (“dissonant ammo”): by completing a chain of story assignments and by completing a series of side quests. Thus, players with different levels of activity (ability to devote time to the game) have a more than realistic chance of getting most of the prizes, even if they did not manage to progress far along the storyline.[/p][p]What could pilots obtain during the adventure:[/p][olist][*][p]By destroying Precursor spies (the easiest enemies in Inverter), you could obtain parts for the “Spiral” (R10) and “Endeavour” (R10) ships, as well as unique weapons for them (“Overheating laser” and “Compression railgun”).

[b]Total: 2 ships + 2 weapons[/b][/p][/*][*][p]By destroying Precursor guardians (the more difficult enemies in the Inverter), active players received parts for the “Gargoyle” (R11), “Dart” (R11), “Raven” (R16), “Dyrnwyn” (R17), as well as parts for the “Th’ak’Len” R5-9 weapon (a unique weapon for the “Waz’Got”).

[b]Total: 4 ships + 1 weapon[/b][/p][/*][*][p]By destroying the “Conquistador’s” turrets (using dissonant ammo or volleys from the “Defiant’s” main weapon), it was possible to assemble “Gungnir” (R16), “Granite” (R16), as well as get parts for the “Th’ak’Len” weapon R8-12 and R11-15, not counting the resources for building ships (xeno- and monocrystals, screened batteries, processing blocks, composite panels, iridium, etc.).

It is worth noting that the loot from the destroyed “Conquistador” turrets was available to almost everyone: 24 out of 32 turrets were destroyed in one volley (even if the volley was fired by one player without “target preparation”). Considering that a standard frigate cargo hold without “extenders” can hold 6 slots, this would be enough for 4 frigates; that is, it was quite possible to collect “leftovers from someone else’s table” (by prior agreement, many would not refuse).

[b]Total: 2 ships + 2 weapons[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Completing the adventure storyline, players received, in addition to ammunition, a unique “Exorcist” (R3) ship, a unique “Aurora” modifier for “Hercules”, a “Snoop” scanner, unique “Thi'Lith” weapons, “Coil Mortar”, and “Tai’thaq”, as well as the “Salamander” (R16) ship. Moreover, everything except the “Salamander” and “Tai’thaq” could be obtained no later than the “Old meetings at the favorite spot” assignment, that is, barely passing ⅔ of the storyline. And although active players received the “Salamander” closer to the finish, it was still at least a week or two before the end of the adventure.

[b]Total: 2 ships + 2 unique modifiers + 3 unique weapons[/b][/p][/*][/olist][p][b]In total[/b], active players were able to collect 10 ships, 8 unique weapons, as well as the “Aurora” and “Snoop” modifiers that are not just “collectibles”, but are also extremely useful in open world and in the PvP arena. We hope that this was a generous enough reward for those who devoted their time to the adventure.[/p][p]We monitored your feedback and saw many comments that the adventure was too long, but it was not just a chain of assignments during which it was impossible to use seed-chips in the open world. The adventure was more of an open world state, during which players had the opportunity to obtain valuable loot. In order for each player to have the opportunity to try out the gameplay of this open world state at their own pace, we decided to make the delay between assignments so “generous”. We repeatedly reduced this delay for older assignments so that everyone would have the opportunity to catch up with the “leaders” as quickly as possible. The total duration was about 4 months; by our standards, it seemed as enough time to engage in an interesting activity during the adventure, as well as to get rich. However, we will try to take your feedback into account and think about a pace that would not seem too fast or too slow.[/p][p]In addition to the somewhat unconventional adventure rewards distribution, we tried to cover a variety of needs.[/p][p]First and foremost, of course, is the “fair challenge”: it is not the number of seed-chips that matters, but the personal skill and ingenuity of the pilots. According to our assessment, the majority of adventure’s stages could be completed on “silver” ships. It was not even necessary to have an “impressive fleet”, and many stages could be completed on low-level “Hercules”, “Lynx-M”, and “Exorcist” ships. And it could be done solo, without gathering a support group, although we did not prevent players from doing so.[/p][p]We tried to make the challenges interesting: players could show off their general knowledge of stars and space, as well as their knowledge of the game lore and the Star Conflict universe. For example, there was a riddle about the “heart of the scorpion”: Arab astronomers called the star Antares “Kalb al-Akrab”, or “Heart of the Scorpion”, the brightest star in that constellation. Or the riddle about the “planet named after a demon” Naberius, etc.[/p][p]New game mechanics: “catch-up” with the Courier, searching and destroying spies, bringing an enemy (which is almost impossible to kill on your own) under turret fire, various ways to find and destroy invisible enemies, and even dissonant ammunition — all of this required not much firepower, but a significant weakening of enemies or an increase in the survivability of your own ship. Most importantly, players were presented with a puzzle: “How can you do it?”[/p][p]Increased player communication: some stages were indeed easier to complete in a group, but it was not necessary to join any corporations or groups; most often it was enough to simply find “friends for 5 minutes”, or ask for a hint on the community’s social pages. We believe that every player had the opportunity to at least join those who were already in the process of completing an assignment.[/p][p][/p][h2]Did the developers’ expectations match the players’ experience?[/h2][p]Partly, yes. But there were also many situations where we planned something one way, but the players behaved completely differently. However, we don’t see this as a bad thing; in fact, it sometimes sparked a lively interest in how else the pilots could complete the planned (and repeatedly tested) scenario of a stage.[/p][p]Here are a few specific examples:[/p][list][*][p]At the very beginning of the adventure, we couldn’t imagine that anyone could destroy even one of the Precursors’ ships in the Inverter without dissonant ammunition. We made them quite tough, but forgot to remove the loot set up for testing, namely, the dissonant ammunition, which was supposed to be obtained only by destroying the spies or through interaction with agents. However, there were some skilled players who defeated the Precursors without any seed-chips or special ammunition, obtained the “dissonant ammo” and began to fight the Guardians. One fine morning, we got a message: “Look, they haven’t killed a single spy yet, but they are already destroying Precursors in the Inverter...” The development team collectively facepalmed and had to make an unscheduled patch.[/p][/*][*][p]No one could have imagined that players would search for Enigma agent in Fort Muerto on destroyers, sweeping away all pirate turrets in their path. We assumed: “Well, they’ll use ships with invisibility... well, they’ll fly past the turrets on high-speed ships, dodging missiles... they’ll hack the turrets... or use guided torpedoes of the Jericho long-range frigates to survey the area from a safe distance...” However, players choose destroyers and violence![/p][/*][*][p]The “Waterworks championship” assignment provided a hint: “a wildcat at dawn will help you”. This referred to the “Lynx-M” with the “Dawn” module... Yes, this setup does not have much firepower, but it is possible to go into invisibility, wait out groups of enemies among the ruins, and with the help of the “Dawn” and the “Snoop” scanner issued the day before, first study the Courier’s route, and then lie in wait for him in places where he circles around buildings or makes long straight flights. However, players went with more direct approach.[/p][/*][*][p]At the Ice Reef (“Step out of the gloom!”), it would seem that you should take the “Exorcist” frigate (with a unique torpedo that sees all invisible enemies and brings them out of invisibility within its range), equip it with the “Snoop” scanner (which shows all invisible enemies at a distance of 7500m (and only invisible ones, even in PvP)), and calmly find the enemy from a safe distance, send a torpedo at them (two or three will be enough to destroy them), and look for the next one. This stage is about methodical and careful extermination. But we left one “loophole”. More precisely, we decided not to make enemies too strong, so that players could escape them in an emergency. And players jumped at this “mercy backdoor”, crowding and beating up the poor spies.[/p][/*][*][p]In one of the stages, it would have been logical to build turrets one by one, securing yourself in a sector safe from local enemies, and then find at least one spy with a torpedo and make him an enemy, inflicting minimal damage. Then you could activate the “Snoop” and use a torpedo to bring the enemy out of invisibility into the turrets’ area of effect from a safe distance. We are not sure if anyone used this strategy.[/p][/*][*][p]Dissonant ammo. Some took them too literally, as “some kind of unguided missile that deals massive damage to Aliens.” As we noticed, few people used the cloud that the torpedo leaves after detonation: it reduces the resistance of enemy ships by 2 times and reduces incoming damage to the torpedo owner’s ship by 75%. Only 1-2 players could create “clouds of dissonance” around distant anti-aircraft guns (which cannot be destroyed with a normal shot, “solo”) befor firing the main weapon of the “Defiant”. Such a simple coordinated action would leave the Precursor ship completely without anti-aircraft guns after the salvo. And if a group of Guardians were lured into the blast wave from the main weapon’s shot...[/p][/*][/list][p]Unfortunately, we have to admit that not all players fully explore the capabilities of new items, whether they are ships or equipment. Or perhaps we did not communicate the key features well enough, which, in our opinion, should have been immediately obvious. For example, few people were interested in the “Exorcist” with its guided torpedo: “Oh well, it’s low-tier, let’s just put it in the collection and forget about it”. However, this torpedo has increased maneuverability and is capable of revealing both players and AI enemies, at a distance comparable to the effects of “Dawn” and “Aurora”. We really hoped that these features would suggest a certain way of playing to pilots, but judging by the feedback, it didn’t quite turn out as expected.[/p][p]Or the “Snoop” scanner, a CPU modifier that is only installed on low-tier ships, is essentially a version of the “Spatial scanner”. It helps to detect invisible (and only invisible, without cluttering the UI) enemies at a distance of 7.5 km in both the open world and any other mode, including PvP Arena. And in open world sectors it can help you find mysterious “blue” containers with Mk.5 blueprints. This scanner becomes available to players after completing the stage “Unlawful son and mother of all stars”, that is, in the middle of the adventure storyline. Perhaps for the sake of this one item alone (not counting the harder to obtain “Th’ak’Len”, the “Aurora” scanner, and the “Exorcist” ship), it was worth taking your time to complete at least half of the adventure, and the scanner itself was tied to the optimal completion of a number of further stages.[/p][p]We also would like to talk about the adventure guides made by the players themselves. Our entire team would like to express our respect to TheDerpNukem, DarkWind56, and all the other players who actively helped other pilots progress through the assignments. Initially, we were skeptical about such initiatives, believing that they deprived players of the opportunity to solve puzzles on their own. However, over time, we realized that those who want to play on their own will not rely heavily on guides and walkthroughs. The fact is that initially, a hint system was planned to help players complete a particular assignment in case they got “stuck”, but for a number of technical reasons, it had to be abandoned. As it turned out, all the pilots who helped their comrades unwittingly became our “freelance assistants”, increasing the level of player communication, which was one of the goals of the adventure. Even if the walkthroughs shared by the players turned out to be different from what we had in mind, they still worked and helped to progress through the chain of assignments.[/p][p]Once again, we would like to express our gratitude and respect to all authors of guides and walkthroughs, as well as those who offered a helping hand in completing difficult stages directly in the game![/p][p][/p][h2]What were the challenges in the development of the adventure?[/h2][p]All the difficulties stemmed from the fact that the game’s engine is already quite old, and a number of necessary mechanics were simply not included during development. We couldn’t implement some simple (by today’s standards) things or ideas simply because they weren’t there in the first place, and reworking that would require major changes to the code. A simplified and exaggerated example: let’s say you built a house and you need to remove/add/change just a few bricks near the floor. To maintain the integrity and reliability of the structure, you would have to dismantle the house almost down to its foundations and rebuild it again, which sometimes makes it more optimal to build a new house and solve the issue of “replacing bricks” in a roundabout way or postpone it.[/p][p]Some things simply could not be taken into account from the start. For example, the problem with the “Kim was here” stage and the pursuit of the courier at “Naberia-392 complex”. We simply exceeded the once-set (and long-forgotten) limit on the number of stages in the adventure, which turned out to be critical at the moment when the courier was lost and reset, and this error could not be detected during testing. Yes, the problem was eventually solved, and the players were returned to the correct stage, but of course this spoiled the overall experience somewhat.[/p][p]The same applies to pirate destroyers. Yes, the fact that they “leave” after a while has been a long-standing mechanic, and within the scenarios where it was applied, everything looked relatively normal and logical. But in the stages of the adventure, such an “exodus” looked a bit strange, we agree. However, it was decided not to rework this, in order to leave the possibility of completing the stage for those who, for some reason, could not enlist the help of other pilots. As a result, the stage turned out to be logically inaccurate.[/p][p]It is also worth talking about the seed-chips. They introduce a fairly large imbalance, greatly simplifying the game in open world. AI enemies are no longer any competition, and assignments such as “collect valuables” and “find/destroy” become practically monotonous: in the first case, you need to fly close to an object and press the interaction button, and in the second, fly within shooting range and press the fire button. Under such conditions, any challenge completely disappears. We understand that there are players who are satisfied with this gameplay, but as practice has shown, disabling the seed-chips does not critically affect the ability to complete assignments. Yes, it becomes more difficult in some systems, especially in the Jericho sectors, but the opportunity to complete any contract still remains. As mentioned earlier, there were even skilled players who were able to destroy new enemies in the Inverter without dissonant ammunition! However, there is another aspect of the open world that is much more affected by disabling the seed-chips: PvP. In this case, the conditions for players are equivalent to those in the PvP Arena or any other PvP mode, which significantly reduces the “gap” between owners of chips of different quality and increases the risk of return fire, which must now be taken into account.[/p][p]Naturally, during activities related to the open world (in particular, this adventure), a huge gap in capabilities is created if the chips are not disabled, whereas our goal was for players to start out on relatively equal footing and achieve results based on their current skills and quick thinking rather than because they once got a rare BFG. Seed-chips were introduced into the game quite a long time ago, and over that time our attitude towards them has become rather the opposite, but we are not ready to completely remove them either: many players have spent a significant amount of resources and time on them, and it would be unfair to just get rid of them. So if you value your seed-chips, don’t worry, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to use them![/p][p][/p][h2]What are the future plans for utilizing the experience gained during the adventure?[/h2][p]Significant work needs to be done to communicate certain aspects and descriptions to players in a more understandable way, so that people can quickly and correctly understand what the developers are offering them.[/p][p]Regarding seed-chips, it is possible (we cannot promise when, returning to the example with the bricks) that chips will be disabled in the current static PvP sectors of the open world, but will still work in PvE sectors. The task is not easy, but we are considering ways to implement it.[/p][p]Moving slightly away from the topic to the 18+ rank ships, discussions are ongoing. In general, we have no desire to create more ranks. Of course, the introduction of new ranks will generate increased interest in them, but this is more of a “race to nowhere.” The game already has a huge number of both old and not-so-old ships with interesting and sometimes unique mechanics, but they have been undeservedly forgotten. Some may have noticed that many activities are now focused on trying to “rehabilitate” low-rank (mostly “silver”) ships with minimal participation of “purple” and R16-17 ships. In particular, this adventure could be completed quite efficiently with standard ships, which we checked repeatedly, and for some difficult cases, ships and modules were issued free of charge, allowing players to complete a whole chain of stages.[/p][p]Either way, we value the opinions of players, and if we notice a demand for them, then based on the results of surveys, we may consider introducing ships of 18+ ranks... And “insurance” against anomalies![/p]

notes.title: Epilogue. Part 5. Hope
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/d5d4cf44e905b306bfab4771e87d692235c73876.jpg"][/img][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509588921973211147"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509588921973211770"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509589459369459756"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509589459369460070"][/dynamiclink][/p][hr][/hr][p]The Jericho fleet was leaving the meeting point and, in fact, the entire space known to the Empire and the Federation. Bartle once again led his people into the unknown. This time, however, they were not branded criminals and religious fanatics in the eyes of the people, but valiant albeit temporary comrades-in-arms. The Mendes family expressed a desire to remain in the Frontier sectors, Bartle left the Liu family with orders to guard Jericho-3, and the Custodians were to maintain order in the former Jericho sectors. The Emperor, who up until the last moment was ready to give the order to attack Jericho’s fleet in case of aggression, was glad that Bartle had acted wisely and that he would not have to lose half of the remnants of the Imperial fleet for the sake of an old grudge.[/p][p]A few minutes after the Jericho fleet left the sector, two ships emerged from warp: a small yacht and a cargo ship. The young and beautiful guest quickly made her way to the Emperor’s cabin. The Emperor nodded to her, and she stood to his right in front of the huge screen. Everything was done quickly, and remote control of a special compartment in the cargo hold of the second ship was successfully established.[/p][p]“Open the container,” ordered the Emperor, and the automatic system obeyed him, bringing out the biomorph that had been frozen in the cargo ship.[/p][p]The Emperor waited a few minutes for the creature to thaw, then turned on the microphone and said:[/p][p]“I demand communication.”[/p][p]The creature did not even flinch, as expected, so the Emperor repeated the same phrase in the language of the Precursors. The biomorph instantly ceased its chaotic behavior. Now it listened attentively to one of the rulers of the galaxy.[/p][p]“We have destroyed your former masters,” said the Emperor, “and now we are strong. I offer you the chance to leave our territory.”[/p][p]“Innn yourrr cuuultureee, it is cusssstomaryyy to giiiive sooomethhhhing in rrrreturrrrn,” the biomorph slowly growled, giving the impression that the Bione controlling it did not fully understand the concept of words. “Wwhyyyy ssshoooould weee giiive uuuup ourrrr plaanssss?”[/p][p]“I am giving you, or more precisely, the Bione who is currently controlling this body,” said the Emperor, “a safe passage and supplies of iridium to reach other parts of the galaxy, and I will stop the charged weapon that destroyed your brother who attacked humanity. In return, I demand that you return what you took from me. I will know your answer by your actions.”[/p][p]The biomorph froze, the Emperor turned off the screen and finally leaned back in his chair for the first time in three days. Ms. Summer looked at him with her black eyes and saw his exhaustion.[/p][p]“What do you want back from them?” asked one of the Revenants’ leaders.[/p][p]“Hope,” said the Emperor. “Now that I have a few interesting things from the former masters of the Galaxy, I can restore hope. The way they manipulated minds allows us to extract the human part from a biomorph and then place it in a clone that is free of the Liu virus. Especially if it is a ‘wild’ biomorph and no Bione protects its brain from such actions.”[/p][p]Soon, Ms. Summer left the Emperor’s flagship, already knowing what name she would take next. She shared the Emperor’s hope that humanity would manage to leave the Black Abyss of forgotten stars and reclaim what belonged to them by right. This hope was shared by Bartle, who eavesdropped on the conversation between the Emperor and Ms. Summer from his ark rushing through the vastness of the universe, realizing that saving even a small fraction of people affected by the Liu virus would be a huge breakthrough.[/p]

notes.title: Star Conflict 1.13.9а. The 11th anniversary!
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/6ea843201ae2aafd7b36cf018e69298331f4bca7.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Eleven years ago, on September 4, 2014, Star Conflict was officially released. Since then, the world of the project has changed significantly. For eleven years, pilots have been fighting each other in PvP battles, completing assignments in PvE missions, and exploring Open Space.[/p][p]During this time, new fighters, frigates, and destroyers joined the game’s fleet. New weapons and modules have been developed. New locations have been discovered.[/p][p]Over the past year, many unique ships have been introduced into the game. “Helios” borrowed the modularity of destroyers, equipping itself with upgrades that expand its capabilities, and its unique weapons allowed it to control the battlefield like never before. “Psiloi” flew into the space battlefields with a unique special module that summons powerful propulsion systems. “Bashe” inherited the flexibility of “Salamander”, but in the form of a destroyer. “Persei-8” brought a bit of nostalgia, along with formidable capabilities of a tackler. “Drag'Thir” has shown that Ellydium continues to create exceptional ships based on crystallid technology. “Hellas” expanded the line of classic-looking ships, alongside “Bark-2”. “Amber” demonstrated the power of stationary tacklers. “Exorcist” helped bring enemies out of the shadows with its unique special module. Finally, “Cinquedea” has found its way to some pilots who are now looking for the best ways to use this ECM interceptor.[/p][p]Over the past year, modes such as “Orion’s belt” and “Beetle in the Anthill” have become available in Custom Battle, allowing players to enjoy themselves in these unique gameplay scenarios. However, some of the fun had to be toned down a bit: “Temple of last hope” had its maximum mission duration cut by 30 minutes.[/p][p]A few months ago, we launched an experimental monthly rotation of maps and modes for the highest-ranked ships in the PvP Arena. Although the total number of map and mode combinations has been reduced by about 30%, we hope this has helped stabilize the gameplay experience by removing maps and modes that didn't fit well with the current game balance. In the latest rotation, we reduced the number of available maps and modes even further to better shape the optimal gameplay, and the upcoming rotation will offer a similar set of combinations.[/p][p]Perhaps the biggest event of the year was the “Return of the Precursors” adventure, held in the Open World. Even before it began, we launched “The Frontier Voice” to hint at what you might expect in the near future within the game’s lore. Some things were true, some were meant to confuse, but the intrigue remained until the adventure was announced. Amidst all the hype, the “Atlas” corporation has quietly appeared, a new weapons factory that has already released a whole range of unique equipment. But when the Precursors began their invasion, perhaps no one could have imagined that the entire operation would turn out to be so long, exhausting, and... profitable? Yes, the launch of the adventure was not without flaws: as soon as the “Inverter” became available to visit, players discovered a way to obtain unique powerful ammunition, which was more of a bug that was fixed a little later. The adventure itself contained many assignments that often required knowledge of the game, the plot, or astronomy; sometimes you had to “hunt for pixels” in search of “Enigma”; sometimes you had to hunt for spies... However, we are glad that players decided to work together and solve problems jointly, sharing their findings. align="justify"][/p][h2]Festive titles[/h2][p]For the special occasion, we have prepared new unique titles for all pilots. Now you can admire the fireworks and celebrate in various game modes.[/p][p][/p][h2]Special achievement available only during the celebration[/h2][p]For the most remarkable players, we have prepared a special achievement, which can only be obtained during the celebration.[/p][list][*][p]Deal damage with a special anniversary missile volley[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][hr][/hr][h1]The mysterious anomaly returns[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/c2558332e9dc76d900d858499fa13bce37694013.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Pilots, according to UMC intelligence, the operation of seed-chips may still be at risk due to the presence of the Signal.[/p][p]Excerpt from Dr. Leo Gins' report: "Seed-chips are anisotropic structures by their very nature. To spontaneously destroy such a structure, some internal energy is required. The Signal field provides just that. This is a classic case of a second-order phase jump. The particles that make up the crystal structure of a seed-chip acquire additional accessible states, and a certain quantum process occurs, suggesting that the most probable state is one where the crystal structure is isotropic. notes.title: Epilogue. Part 4. Behind the curtain
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/9b04b66048ce3b928301d425edfdcf06ecad2a76.jpg"][/img][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509588921973211147"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509588921973211770"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509589459369459756"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509590093865943500"][/dynamiclink][/p][hr][/hr][p]When the Emperor went to his cabin, the first thing he did was call the Blackwood corporation executives. The smiling clerks began to tell him how happy they were to see him back. The Emperor listened to them for a couple of minutes, then asked to speak with Ariadne. The joy vanished from the faces of the corporation’s directors. [/p][p]“I plan to invest a large sum in the shipyards,” the Emperor said to Ariadne. “I need dozens, hundreds, maybe thousands of heavy cruisers. In return, I will not prevent you from further expanding your influence. I will even turn a blind eye to the presence of a ship’s assistant named Ariadne in my territories. In return, I demand only one thing: loyalty.”[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]At the same moment, Bartle was talking to his Oracles:[/p][p]“Jericho’s main mission here is complete. We need to gather the remnants of our battered fleet, repair the arks we have left, and retreat to the periphery of the galaxy, far from the gaze of the Empire and the Federation, who are now stronger than us. Right now, the only thing holding the Emperor back from attacking us is the fact that the Federation would definitely be able to destroy his fleet if he got involved in another war. So, I order you to gather the Raid and all the Families that are ready to leave. We will set out in a few days. The desire to remain in the Frontier sectors is not encouraged, but I have never taken away your right to choose.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Meanwhile, the Federation was discussing a possible war with the Empire and Jericho at the same time. One of the ministers said:[/p][p]“They have a perfect excuse to start a war: the Vanguard’s information about the Precursor sector has led to iridium fever and war with the Aliens. And the Emperor, since he has, perhaps temporarily, united with Bartle, will find leverage over our people by starting a real war, which we may not win. What’s more, almost eight percent of the Armada was lost in completing a ‘private’ contract. Who accepted it in the first place? Why do we find out that, albeit for fabulous sums of money, a significant part of our fleet was fighting for the interests of the Emperor and Bartle only when the battle is over? Who could have pulled this off?!”[/p][p]The Federation’s chief information security expert said:[/p][p]“I managed to find out something. Apparently, a TV presenter named Marcus Chromakeykus was involved, but it seems that the wrong person was contacted. And it looks like the unfreezing of the Eternal Vanguard unit is connected with this contract.”[/p][p]The name of this individual caused some of the ministers to burst into hysterical laughter, and the Minister of Information Security realized that this might very well be his last day in office. However, none of those present in the room had any idea that the “mistress” of this TV presenter was currently demanding to speak with the Emperor.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]“I was just about to contact you, my dearest friend,” said the Emperor mockingly to the owner of the legendary black dreadnought. “It seems that you are no longer ‘hate’, but ‘summer’? Well, it doesn’t matter, as you can see, I have achieved my goals. And for destroying our common enemy, I will require a small gift from you. I need to talk to someone... unusual.”[/p][p]“I won’t hide my joy that the master of the Black Abyss is finally dead,” said Ms. Summer, then asked her old acquaintance:[/p][p]“Why did you hide everything from my Order when you knew that we wish only death upon the Precursors?”[/p][p]“There is at least one among the Biones who is still loyal to the Precursors,” replied the Emperor. “The horrors on Earth, as you understand, are his doing. But there was another in league with him, fortunately for us, he is no longer. I couldn’t take any chances, so I contacted you at the last moment. You have no idea how hard it was to hide from Bartle that you were involved in our operation in the Nith system. Now back to business. Is the Crystallids’ machine still not accessible to anyone?”[/p][p]“If we don’t count your friend Kathleen, you’re the only one who has reached the Fringe and become like one of the Precursors, the more adequate ones,” said Summer.[/p][p]“That’s a shame,” she added sadly, “it would have been much more convenient than my method of immortality with clones or Bartle’s almost complete cybernetization. I’ll find a gift for you. Wait for a delivery. Just let me listen to the recording afterwards.”[/p][p]“You can watch it live if you come in person,” said the Emperor, “and one last question: do you still have any partially unfrozen personalities from the Vanguard that could be useful if negotiations with the Federation don’t go according to plan?”[/p]

notes.title: Epilogue. Part 3. Freedom
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/296bd160c68b989ac5e3a7ec1e7ddbce6dc29a3a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509588921973211147"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509588921973211770"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509589459369460070"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509590093865943500"][/dynamiclink][/p][hr][/hr][p]“So, my loyal generals,” said the Emperor to the assembled senior officers and leaders of the Empire’s factions. “It is impossible to restore the Empire to its pre-Invasion state. Therefore, I offer you the following solution: each of you has proven your worth and the quality of your approach, and so you will retain almost complete control over your territories. The Senate will retain its functions and freedom of action. I will only intervene in this matter if I deem it necessary. Anticipating your questions, I will answer: I could not return or declare my existence earlier, otherwise the fate of Earth would have befallen any place where I appeared openly. Now this threat has passed with the death of the Precursors. And yes, what happened in the Solar system is yet another misdeed of the former masters of the Galaxy, who even in stasis managed to destroy worlds.”[/p][p]“I beg your pardon, Your Highness,” asked Ironside, “but what shall we do with Warren? He controls Sterpefeid and is completely disloyal to you.”[/p][p]“We’ll deal with that right now,” the Emperor replied with a slight smile, and gave an order: “Connect us with the leader of that... what’s it called... the Great Empire.”[/p][p]A call to Alfred Warren was made, and he appeared on the screen. The usually arrogant and self-confident general turned pale. He turned even paler when the Emperor asked him:[/p][p]“They say you are no longer loyal to me. Is that true?”[/p][p]Warren managed to gather his will and reply, “Yes. I am no longer loyal to you. The Great Empire will go its own way, and you have no choice but to respect its freedom. Otherwise, you will pointlessly kill billions of those you consider your citizens. My people will defend their home, Sterpefeid, from you at any cost. I will never forget how you destroyed one of our planets.”[/p][p]The Emperor paused for a moment, not revealing that he had already made up his mind, then said:[/p][p]“So, Warren, you want freedom. Well, you and the former Sterpefeid will have it. And you won’t even suffer the fate of Skifia.”[/p][p]The Emperor’s words were surprising, but he continued his speech, pressing a button on his panel, after which an alarm siren sounded on Warren’s side.[/p][p]“So, first things first. Right now, I have disabled the warp stream stabilizers that made your region convenient for travel. Without them, warp storms will destroy half of your communications with other sectors and states within a month. The remaining channels will become even more expensive to maintain. You will let those who wish to leave your Great Empire go. Moreover, our conversation is now being broadcast on all your terminals, which you have so thoughtfully placed on every corner of your territory. I disabled the warp stream stabilizers for a simple reason: they are feeding on resources from other parts of the Empire, which you received free of charge under one of the old agreements. And I now consider that agreement null and void. So, I offer you the freedom of choice: return to the central authority of the Empire and become part of our state again, or continue your attempts to build your own Empire. But in the second case, do not count on my leniency, and, of course, all Wardens’ tech will be dismantled from the sector, including the weapon you hate so much. I give you a week to think about it.”[/p][p]“Freedom!” Warren shouted. “I choose freedom, we don’t need your handouts!”[/p][p]“So be it,” replied the Emperor, after which silence hung in the room.[/p][p]The Emperor glanced at one of the folders on the table, then demanded a call with two parties: Sparta and the Republic of Separate Worlds.[/p][p]“Now, I have a number of complaints against the Republic of Separate Worlds,” said the Emperor. “Not only are you attacking Sparta, but you are also damaging space stabilizers, which leads to increased activity of the Aliens in the systems near Pandora. Stop this, and we can begin negotiations on the status of your territories. I may forgive you for past grievances, but new ones... Open a communication channel with the Alliance.”[/p][p]“We assumed you were alive,” said the Federation’s foreign minister. “Do you want some kind of negotiations?”[/p][p]“Yes,” replied the Emperor. “I agree to recognize the Republic of Separate Worlds, but if they show aggression towards my citizens...”[/p][p]“That will be their own business if they wish to commit suicide in this manner,” replied the minister. “Please tell me, do you have any other constructive proposals?”[/p][p]“Yes,” replied the Emperor, cutting off communication with Sparta and the Republic of Separate Worlds. “A new trade agreement and some proposals for joint control of dangerous territories. My representatives will send it to you shortly.”[/p]

notes.title: Epilogue. Part 2. Speech for the fleet
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/30627d01bbdd105dc480f0448b790b277caeaf5a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509588921973211147"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509589459369459756"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509589459369460070"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509590093865943500"][/dynamiclink][/p][hr][/hr][p]A huge fleet gathered at a single point, awaiting orders. However, there were almost a third fewer ships than just a short time ago, and the recently neat hulls of the dreadnoughts, cruisers, and destroyers were now crisscrossed with cracks and holes, and in some cases entire sections were missing. Repairs were in full swing, as the participants in the recent battle did not yet know that they had won. They did not realize even when space changed colors; on the contrary, many fingers trembled on the triggers.[/p][p]At one point, the flagship emerged from warp. It looked terrible: the hull was melted in many places, but the multi-layered armor had done its job and saved the ship’s interior and crew. However, there was a lot of damage visible to the naked eye that affected the ship’s important systems: the engine nozzles were bent, and a third of them were clearly out of order. The main weapon, capable of piercing a planet’s crust, was torn apart, and one of the ship’s compartments resembled a sieve, with dozens of holes the size of a small frigate, slowly being mended by repair modules, at least from the outside. It was not apparent, but the damage to the ship was much more extensive than it appeared, and half the crew was eagerly trying to repair countless breakages in each of the sectors of the vessel.[/p][p]The Emperor and Bartle exchanged glances, and the leader of Jericho yielded to his colleague, as the more public figure, the right to begin their speech. Only one of the many scenarios assumed that the soldiers would ever hear these words, since in the majority of the calculated outcomes, either the flagship or the fleet would not survive. And so, under the frenzied flickering of space visible even from the farthest ship, the Emperor began his speech:[/p][p]“We are victorious! I congratulate you on your triumph in this battle. Our united fleet prevented the Aliens from coming to the aid of our enemies, the Precursors themselves. Because of this, the allied forces of Ellydium in the Nith system, supported by the UMC mercenaries, were able to accomplish their mission and slightly damage the Precursor flagship’s defense systems. This proved sufficient to render them vulnerable to their own weapons, which were supposed to protect their temporary resting place. Right now, the former masters of the Galaxy are on the receiving end of what they once did to dozens of intelligent species. Bartle and I believe that our fleet deserves to know the truth about the battle. Our enemies were the creators of the Biones and biomorphs. The Liu virus and many other horrors that tormented and still terrify the Galaxy are the work of their twisted minds.”[/p][p]The founder of the Fringe and the creator of Jericho continued: “Many years ago, there were two nations that we now call the Precursors. One of them found a way to merge several minds together, while the other considered this sacrilegious. Both peoples explored the Galaxy, each creating a tool to suit themselves: one created the Crystallids, the other the Biones. At some point, they created the Signal to find other civilizations in the Galaxy and offer them an alliance, or at least to learn about potential enemies in advance. And one day, someone responded. Responded to their diplomacy with an attack. The Precursors suffered losses and could not bear the insult, so they turned their tools into weapons and won both the battle and the war. But they did not stop there. The Signal became a beacon that lured civilizations that believed its message, like sheep to slaughter. Judging by what we have found, the Precursors wiped out at least fifty-seven intelligent civilizations from the Galaxy. However, the two Precursor nations then became enemies and, for reasons unknown to us, fell into decline. The Biones rebelled against their masters, but the Crystallids remained loyal. We don’t know how, but the Precursors found themselves on the brink of destruction. The Crystallids built a refuge for both nations outside our world, where the Precursors were to hide and prepare their forces for a return to the Galaxy. But the creators of the Biones damaged the refuge of the other nation, contaminating it with what we now know as the Liu virus, and their brothers, unaware of this treachery, did not have time to fight back. The traitors were able to hide in a refuge carefully guarded by the Crystallids and the Leviathan, a Bione on the Crystallids’ leash. They did not know that the backup key to their refuge had been preserved. And we took advantage of it, throwing them out of the place where they had been gathering their strength. We avenged the countless civilizations that our enemies had destroyed, tearing the Precursors from their invulnerable refuge and ending our enemy’s existence with their own weapons. And now, my brothers and sisters, I will tell you why the Fringe became Jericho. As soon as my oracles and I learned what happened in the Galaxy because of the Precursors, we changed our goal somewhat. Our new secret mission was not only to find the creators of the Signal, but also to prevent them from destroying humanity. And Jericho succeeded in this endeavor.”[/p][p]When each of the rulers of the Galaxy finished their first short speech, they gave the order for the fleets to undergo routine repairs before leaving the sector in a few weeks.[/p]

notes.title: Epilogue. Part 1. The Last Minutes
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/daf5cd341a77e39c06679b80456cb7fdeac6fae0.jpg"][/img][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509588921973211770"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509589459369459756"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509589459369460070"][/dynamiclink][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/212070/view/509590093865943500"][/dynamiclink][/p][hr][/hr][p]The Imperial flagship, accompanied by thirty Imperial and a dozen Jericho dreadnoughts, was fighting off the never-ending hordes of Aliens at the most intense sector of the battle. The shield generators of each of the ships have given out multiple times already, and there were numerous holes left on each United Fleet ship’s hull by the enemy fire. The smaller stations set up in space were seemingly less affected. The Aliens considered them much less of a threat. The flagship’s bridge was filled with officers, and the Emperor and Bartle were personally overseeing the rebuilding of the constantly crumbling blockade of the Nith system as the two most experienced admirals in the galaxy. The task was not made easier by the ongoing barrage of urgent messages. [/p][p align="justify"]“Your Highness, the third squadron needs support, we can’t hold on much longer.”[/p][p align="justify"]“The AD-∑-14 formation will now follow the ‘Eternity’ protocol. It was an honor to serve the Jericho.”[/p][p align="justify"]“The ‘Typhon’ squad retreats to regroup.”[/p][p align="justify"]“Do not retreat, hold positions, sending out reinforcements in one minute.”[/p][p align="justify"]The entire power of the fleets of two of the three strongest states in the galaxy, as well as a third of the fleet of the third state, could not cope with the attacks of the Aliens. The Defilers, Destroyers, Hunters, and Predators were restricted by heavy warp stream destabilizers and could not get close to the Inverter, but even a well-prepared defense was no match for their sheer numbers and firepower. Space was filled with the wreckage of human and Alien ships, becoming a mass grave for millions of people and Precursor drones.[/p][p align="justify"]Many did not understand why the right to battle the Precursor flagship had been given to the Ellydium dreadnought and the mercenaries, rather than to the Ark or the Emperor’s ship, which had greater firepower. The answer to this question would soon become clear. Amidst the battle, almost no one noticed a small Imperial communications ship emerging from warp. However, the one who has lived more than a thousand years old was feeling impatient today, and noticed it a few seconds later and demanded to open a communications channel before the arriving ship’s systems had adjusted to the sector.[/p][p align="justify"]“Legate Cortés, I demand immediate report,” said the Emperor.[/p][p align="justify"]“We are following the plan, Your Highness,” responded Natasha Cortés, delicately remaining silent about the fact that she was no longer formally a legate of the Imperial Security. “The Ellydium dreadnought partially damaged the target systems. Your ‘gift’ has been delivered to its destination. It seems that our enemies have not noticed it yet.”[/p][p align="justify"]“Perfect,” said the Emperor. “All ships, prepare to jump to rendezvous point ‘Psi-14’ on my command. I authorize the retreat of damaged units. Proceed with the rescue of personnel from immobilized ships. Communication group commanders, relay my order to other sectors of the blockade. Report when ready to jump. In case of risk of ship damage, I authorize you to leave the battlefield without further orders.”[/p][p align="justify"]Bartle only had a few words for his Families and Raid: “Carry out his order.” Many were surprised by the unexpected order, but there were no crazy daredevils who wanted to continue fighting the Aliens. All of those had perished by that time. The Emperor knew that not all the people from the damaged and destroyed ships could be saved, so after half an hour, he gave the order to retreat to the entire fleet, except for the flagship.[/p][p align="justify"]“Kathleen, your time has come,” he said to the one known only to a handful of people in the galaxy. “Activate the device.”[/p][p align="justify"]“Your Highness, I know what I must do,” the girl responded. “Will you be able to leave the system in time if something goes wrong?”[/p][p align="justify"]“Don’t worry,” said the Emperor to the Sleeper. “Turn on the Precursors’ gizmo, it’s time to use their weapon against them.”[/p][p align="justify"]When Lady Kathleen uttered the first words of the Precursor language, the voice activation protocols revived the ancient device, and the Signal intensified, initiating what people had called the Cataclysm ten years ago, and which had been completely forgotten amid the war with the Aliens and other horrors: the cleansing protocol that destroyed all life in Sector 1337, the Precursor sector, every few days. Iridium began to glow, the color of the surrounding space changed, and if anyone had tried to describe what was happening, they would have realized that the very fabric of space at that moment was fluctuating as much as it would near two merging black holes.[/p]

notes.title: Developer blog. Entry 121. Storm season
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/97001f38fddbc72486908acca4eafbf70bda047b.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]The “UMC Archives: Storm season” event[/h2][p]Soon, the next event “UMC Archives: Storm season” will become available to all pilots. It will include a special battle pass, consisting of only one stage and lasting approximately one month. The event itself will run in parallel with the main battle pass “Tales of the ancients” and will end in the beginning of September.[/p][p]All pilots who complete the new “UMC Archives: Storm season” event will be able to get a new Jericho rank 16 ECM interceptor “Cinquedea”, as well as the modules and weapons of this ship. And those who buy pass packs will get additional bundles of resources, seed-chips and ammunition. You will be able to find them in most of the battle pass levels. We will share more details about the contents of the levels with you during the start of the event. The offer is limited in time and will be available until September 18.[/p][p][/p][h2]New ship “Cinquedea”[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/4d8fde94ad77993601c254ccb92c8580167e47b4.jpg"][/img][/p][p]At the middle of August, all pilots will have access to the new Jericho ECM interceptor “Cinquedea”.[/p][p][/p][p]“Cinquedea” is a Sentinels’ ECM interceptor created by implementing various shipbuilding technologies. The Sentinels used their enormous computing power to optimize the adaptation of these technologies, resulting in a highly effective machine.[/p][p]Jericho has always strived to uphold tradition, but in the end, the faction valued effectiveness above all else, and therefore was never afraid to apply innovation in shipbuilding. The Techs were able to convey this idea to the Sentinels. They were “inspired” (if this word can even be applied to the AI) by several ships at once. Firstly, “Zhen”, which already had simple but effective AI nodes and therefore had the software ready to be utilized by the Sentinels. Secondly, the appearance of the “Geyser” weapon and the Imperial ship “Loki” became a foundation for the exterior design of the new ship, later named “Cinquedea”. And lastly, the Sentinels were able to make use of the technology from “Mauler” to create the ship’s energy core. Thus, the ship turned out to be a fusion of some of the latest developments in shipbuilding, and the Sentinels had no difficulty with the computing power needed to optimize the equipment for the new ship.[/p][p]Despite the fact that the Sentinels did not actively advertise their ship or talked about its capabilities in public, the number of buyers for the “Cinquedea” was high. The UMC plans to soon offer its mercenaries the opportunity to order the ship for themselves.[/p][p]
[/p]

Due to the small size of the playing area and relatively open spawn points, it is often possible to see strong and highly mobile ships rushing to occupy the opposing team’s spawn points as quickly as possible. notes.title: New packs “Star Conflict: Amber”
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/52d1386e5413d892899e063df412b61b1c52a81e.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Pilots! The new packs “Star Conflict. Amber” and “Star Conflict: Amber. Deluxe edition” are now available in the official project store. The deluxe pack will be available for purchase until September 18. The ship will be available to all pilots without time limits.
[/p][hr][/hr][h2]Star Conflict: Amber. Deluxe edition[/h2][p][b]This pack includes:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Unique rank 16 tackler fighter “Amber”[/p][/*][*][p]Unique weapon “Amber A15”[/p][/*][*][p]Active module “Drop” active defence[/p][/*][*][p]Unique portrait “Dobrynya, son of Vseslav”[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Additionally, the pilot receives:[/b][/p][list][*][p]10% bonus to credits gain for 90 days[/p][/*][*][p]Unique pattern “Kittens uprising”[/p][/*][*][p]Unique animated decor “K9”[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Additionally, the pilot receives the modules:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Unique shield modifier “Defence systems configurator”[/p][/*][*][p]Unique CPU modifier “Chance” computing adapter[/p][/*][*][p]Active module “Target Painter”[/p][/*][*][p]Active module “Shield Booster M”[/p][/*][*][p]Active module “Engine Suppressor”[/p][/*][*][p]Engine modifier “Inertial Stabilizer”[/p][/*][*][p]Capacitor modifier “Emergency Barrier”[/p][/*][*][p]Shield modifier “Auxiliary Shield Projector”[/p][/*][*][p]Shield modifier “Energy Recuperation System”[/p][/*][*][p]Hull modifier “Reinforced Beams”[/p][/*][*][p]CPU modifier “Horizon” module[/p][/*][*][p]CPU modifier “Overclocked CPU”[/p][/*][/list][p]Special bonus for everyone who buys the bundle — Premium license for 90 days![/p][p][/p][h2]Star Conflict: Amber[/h2][p][b]This pack includes:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Unique rank 16 tackler fighter “Amber”[/p][/*][*][p]Unique weapon “Amber A15”[/p][/*][*][p]Active module “Drop” active defence[/p][/*][*][p]Unique portrait “Dobrynya, son of Vseslav”[/p][/*][/list][p]Special bonus for everyone who buys the bundle — Premium license for 30 days![/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]After the success of “Bashe”, the Seventh Squadron was able to accumulate enough finances to order special equipment from three corporations at once: Helion Inc, Blackwood, and, as rumor has it, the Sentinels. None of the parties could clearly infer the purpose of the devices ordered, but the Sentinels suspected they were for a tackler ship, as they used similar nodes to outfit “Singularity” platforms with their computing circuits.[/p][p]Soon after, the Seventh Squadron announced a joint project with Gabriel Hugot. The code name for the project was “Amber”. The prototype ship was appropriately named Automatic Multitask Battle Electronic Recon Ship-1 (Amber-S1). Unlike the previous ship of the Seventh Squadron, the first launch did not get much publicity, because, according to the designers and project managers, it is not required for a tackler ship.[/p][p]However, rumors of found wrecks of cyber ships destroyed by unknown weapons soon leaked into the net. The UMC hopes to acquire the right to purchase the ship for its mercenaries in the near future, as well as to obtain the relevant documentation. The UMC’s relentless pursuit of the “Amber” shows that the ship, capable of causing its enemies to freeze, is worth the effort and may be nicknamed after precious fossilized resin for a reason.[/p][p]
[/p]

Recharges after activation.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][hr][/hr][h1]New modules by the “Atlas” Weapon Factories[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/7cd7f202ed3624f686fb7b1c769853c56f42f55c.jpg"][/img][/p][p]“Atlas” is a new corporation that recently entered the weapons market. There is some reason to believe that the corporation uses mostly basic civilian components to assemble the weapons, achieving high performance with a few high-tech parts. Since the fate of Earth is not fully known at this point, there can be no evidence of such a connection.[/p][p]The new battle pass “Tales of the ancients” has three brand-new modules for you. notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/cd13f44d24a0fc93157c11b912c83b5d48906994.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Pilots! The new pack “Star Conflict. Elusive Seeker” now available in the [url="https://store.gaijin.net/story.php?title=Star-Conflict_Elusive-Seeker-pack"]official project store[/url]. The new pack will be available for purchase until September 18. The ship will be available to all pilots without time limits.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="E-ZywBzpEY0;full"][/previewyoutube][p][b]This pack includes:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Rank 16 Jericho tackler “Singularity”[/p][/*][*][p]Unique EM weapon “Accelerator gun”[/p][/*][*][p]Active module “Trap mine”[/p][/*][*][p]Unique CPU modifier “Drone booster”[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Additionally, the pilot receives:[/b][/p][list][*][p]10% bonus to credits gain for 90 days[/p][/*][*][p]Unique title “Polyphemos’ bludgeon”[/p][/*][*][p]Unique pattern “Solar wind”[/p][/*][*][p]Unique decor “Star trackball”[/p][/*][*][p]A set of colours: “Aggressive carmine”, “Iris”, “Daffodil”[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Additionally, the pilot receives ammo:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Dissonant charges — 15 pcs.[/p][/*][*][p]Crystal drone — 15 pcs.[/p][/*][*][p]“Radiation fog” missile — 15 pcs.[/p][/*][*][p]“Doomsday” missile — 15 pcs.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Additionally, the pilot receives the modules:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Active module “Sentry Drone”[/p][/*][*][p]Active module “Target Painter”[/p][/*][*][p]Active module “Shield Booster M”[/p][/*][*][p]CPU modifier “Spatial scanner”[/p][/*][*][p]Engine modifier “Catalyst Injector”[/p][/*][*][p]Engine modifier “Cruise Engine Modification”[/p][/*][*][p]Capacitor modifier “Multiphase Generator”[/p][/*][*][p]Capacitor modifier “Voltage Regulator”[/p][/*][*][p]Shield modifier “Adaptive Shield”[/p][/*][*][p]Shield modifier “EM-diffuser” (2 pcs.)[/p][/*][*][p]Hull modifier “Lightweight Hull”[/p][/*][*][p]Hull modifier “Extended Hull”[/p][/*][/list][p]Special bonus for everyone who buys the bundle — Premium license for 30 days![/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]Every mercenary has heard of the mysterious Techs caste within the Jericho. Many have even done jobs for them, but no one has ever seen them face to face. The caste has always been closed off, even from other Jericho members. People say they don’t simply worship machinery, but consider themselves to be one with technology. When the Jericho disappeared along with the Techs, their creations were left behind. Now their former stations are controlled by a network of AI systems that call themselves Sentinels. Their goals and true nature remains a mystery, even to the few remaining Jericho people.[/p][p]Despite AI operating on a completely different level, sentinels still manage to communicate and deal with humans. They have made many contracts with the Mendes family and a number of other factions. Autonomous AI units within powerful combat “Singularity” tacklers are the Sentinels’ emissaries and diplomats. They possess free will and sometimes make contracts with pilots to serve under them.[/p]

notes.title: Star Conflict 1.13.7a Minor changes
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/3601fa1b4b53b1478d4e1ef9a1e7a48426416771.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This update has minor changes and bug fixes. Also, we continue to implement some experiments we have planned for the game this year.[/p][p][/p][h1][hr][/hr]New unique modules for Bark-2[/h1][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/37975cdbe192bff96f3fc42ac3fdfc46a7756936.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Attention pilots! New unique CPU and hull modifiers for the “Bark-2” ship have been added to the game. We advise owners of the “Star Conflict: Bark-2. Deluxe edition” to check in-game mail during the day, you may have already received them.
[/p][p][b]Hull modifier: “Pykrete reinforcement”[/b][/p][list][*][p]Increases the hull’s resistance to all damage and passively restores the hull by a small amount.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]CPU modifier: “Hidden reserves”[/b][/p][list][*][p]Reloads the missile rack when activated and increases the chance of critical damage for all weapons.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1][hr][/hr]Rank 3 Jericho long-range frigate “Exorcist”[/h1][p][/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/30e08293a6d5b1b060aa839dcfd42188d4b88f33.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/8c51ad1e95bbbce4d521892bfc46cb0d8d02f8d7.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/cf5b216aed547ac52c2d4eaa26db33944f194ecd.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/e5d526f813a8ef77af1ed42248306d84e62b024c.jpg"][/img][/carousel][p]During the first war for the Bartle sector, Jericho sought to find an additional way to combat the emerging Empire’s scout ships and their advanced cloaking systems. Since all of Jericho’s low tonnage vessels lacked such a capability at the time, such a ship was sorely needed. However, due to the Empire’s counterattack, the project had to be suspended.[/p][p]Research was resumed shortly after the meeting between the Emperor and Bartle, as even a ship without the strongest firepower in the galaxy could prove useful in a battle against the Precursor spies.[/p][p]A unique missile system was developed specifically for the “Exorcist”. Within a short radius, it can disrupt the operation of cloaking systems of all known ships, as well as new developments in this area. In addition, the missile for this ship was supplemented with a non-standard system of maneuvering engines, significantly increasing its turning speed.[/p][p]This frigate is mass-produced for the Raid fleet as a mainline AI-controlled combat drone, but a few families have decided to sell small exclusive batches to the UMC.[/p][p][/p][p][b]“Exorcist” ship part[/b][/p][list][*][p]Used for production of the ship “Exorcist”[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Special module “Exorcist” guided torpedo[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fires a guided missile that deals thermal damage upon explosion. All ships within a certain distance from the torpedo lose their invisibility.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1][hr][/hr]New weapons and modules for low-rank ships[/h1][p][/p][p]As part of this update, we added several new weapons and modules for low-rank ships that you can get as part of the “Return of the Precursors” adventure.
[/p][p][b]CPU modifier “Snoop” scanner[/b][/p][list][*][p]Increases the critical hit chance and allows you to activate a radar to search for invisible enemies and items (“X” by default)[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Raider “Thi'Lith” beam[/b][/p][list][*][p]Thermal weapon[/p][/*][*][p]A homing charge is fired at each enemy in the line of fire. Ship energy is spent on each enemy apart from the locked target.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Raider coil mortar rank 1–5[/b][/p][list][*][p]Kinetic weapon[/p][/*][*][p]Railgun with explosive projectiles. Projectiles are fired from each weapon barrel in quick succession. The barrel does not fire if it's in the deadzone.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Raider “Tai'thaq” weapon rank 1–5[/b][/p][list][*][p]Kinetic weapon[/p][/*][*][p]Launches a colony of crystalline pseudo-organisms, devouring ship hulls.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1][hr][/hr]New relic blueprints in the open world[/h1][p][/p][p]Pilots! We have updated the loot in the open world, and now each of you has a chance to get new weapon and module blueprints of relic quality.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Weapons:[/b][/p][list][*][p]“Fort-4” launcher[/p][/*][*][p]Drone operator “RepK-2”[/p][/*][*][p]Star blaster[/p][/*][*][p]“Mesimeri” weapon[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Active modules:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Cluster torpedo[/p][/*][*][p]Redirection of energy flows[/p][/*][*][p]Warp gate “Ram-M”[/p][/*][*][p]Front pyro emitter[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Passive modules:[/b][/p][list][*][p]“Cor Vulnus” auxiliary generator[/p][/*][*][p]Weapon booster “Black jack”[/p][/*][*][p]Snake skin[/p][/*][*][p]“Cor Vulnus” proton wall[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1][hr][/hr]PvP Arena maps rotation[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/bccf0ee953521a3f3b662e9216f49316118e9445.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Pilots! [hr][/hr][h1]Unique rank 16 tackler “Amber”[/h1]

[previewyoutube=Wx8rs1i1fqk;full][/previewyoutube]

After the success of “Bashe”, the Seventh Squadron was able to accumulate enough finances to order special equipment from three corporations at once: Helion Inc, Blackwood, and, as rumor has it, the Sentinels. None of the parties could clearly infer the purpose of the devices ordered, but the Sentinels suspected they were for a tackler ship, as they used similar nodes to outfit “Singularity” platforms with their computing circuits.

Soon after, the Seventh Squadron announced a joint project with Gabriel Hugot. The code name for the project was “Amber”. The prototype ship was appropriately named Automatic Multitask Battle Electronic Recon Ship-1 (Amber-S1). Unlike the previous ship of the Seventh Squadron, the first launch did not get much publicity, because, according to the designers and project managers, it is not required for a tackler ship.

However, rumors of found wrecks of cyber ships destroyed by unknown weapons soon leaked into the net. The UMC hopes to acquire the right to purchase the ship for its mercenaries in the near future, as well as to obtain the relevant documentation. The UMC’s relentless pursuit of the “Amber” shows that the ship, capable of causing its enemies to freeze, is worth the effort and may be nicknamed after precious fossilized resin for a reason.

[hr][/hr][h1]New modules by the “Atlas” Weapon Factories[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/4459272/7cd7f202ed3624f686fb7b1c769853c56f42f55c.jpg[/img]

“Atlas” is a new corporation that recently entered the weapons market. The line of exclusive arms it presented has shown itself perfectly in battle, having different capabilities from the standard weapon modifications. There is some reason to believe that the corporation uses mostly basic civilian components to assemble the weapons, achieving high performance with a few high-tech parts. Some speculate about the corporation’s connection to a civilian company that existed on Earth at the time of the Invasion. Since the fate of Earth is not fully known at this point, there can be no evidence of such a connection.

The new battle pass “Tales of the ancients” has three brand-new modules for you:
[list]
[*] Active module “Iapetus” creates a beam in front of the ship. Enemy ships within the beam receive 1000 thermal damage per second.
[*] Active module “Nemesis” creates a beam in front of the ship. Enemy ships within the beam receive 500 kinetic damage per second and can’t use weapons.
[*] Active module “Zeus” creates a beam in front of the ship. Enemy ships within the beam receive 500 electromagnetic damage per second and slow down by 30%.
[/list]

The regular rotation of maps and modes is the point of this experiment. The list of combinations is planned to be updated monthly, offering players new conditions on a regular basis.

Why are such restrictions necessary? At the moment, there is quite a large number of maps and modes combinations available in the “PvP Arena”, and you can often get the same map with a different mode in a row. This could make the game feel like it didn’t have as large a selection of locations, and playing different modes at the same map could get boring. Maps and mode rotation reduces the total number of combinations, which promises players a more varied experience by curating the combinations more carefully.

Within the rotation, the combinations of maps and modes will vary: for some maps, the number of modes may be reduced or increased, and some will be removed from the rotation altogether. This approach will effectively adapt the PvP game environment to new gameplay content such as ships and equipment, eliminating maps and modes combinations that may not seem to fit the current environment.

The rotation is designed to solidify the balance of power, offering a more challenging environment for powerful new ships, while still leaving room for less relevant ones.

The “Artuga” sector locations have received a significant reduction in the available game modes, but the possible combinations should provide the best gameplay on these maps. For example, the “Captain Kidd’s anchorage” map used to appear in “Team battle” mode, but this mode did not offer the best gameplay for this rather open map, placing players from opposing teams quite close to each other, so battles took place more on the outskirts of the map. The “Beacon hunt” mode was chosen as the most suitable for this map, offering fights for points of interest deep within the location.

In addition, the current rotation will bring back such combinations of maps and modes as:
[list]
[*] “Beacon hunt” at the “Northern mining station”;
[*] “Domination” at the “Derelict Stronghold”;
[*] “Domination” at the “Iridium Strand”.
[/list]
We will keep track of the balance of power in the game and your feedback, and will try to provide the most up-to-date list of maps and modes as part of the next rotation.
